01 / LOCAL

Your voice
stays on your computer.

Speech is recognized on your local CPU. Recordings are never uploaded, and neither audio nor transcripts are logged. Once the models and dependencies are set up, dictation works offline.

On-device recognition · No dedicated GPU needed
02 / BILINGUAL

Chinese and English,
in one breath.

Mixed Chinese–English dictation works out of the box. Say Linux, Python or a whole sentence in English without switching recognition languages. Pinyin typing keeps working as usual.

用 Linux，写下新的想法。
03 / IN FLOW

Text appears as you speak,
pauses end sentences.

Interim text follows your voice. When you pause, punctuation is added, spacing between Chinese and English is tidied, and the sentence is committed. Say several sentences in one recording, with no need to confirm each one.

Streaming preview · Per-sentence commit · Local punctuation

04 / A CLEARER VIEW

A familiar input method,
with a cleaner look.

A white rounded candidate panel, soft shadows and a blue highlight that makes the current option easy to spot. Pinyin candidates and voice status share the same light theme.

  • Bundled with the package and enabled on first setup
  • Keeps your custom theme, dark preference and fonts
  • Upgrades never reset your appearance choices

ONE SHORTCUT AWAY.

One shortcut,
a new way to write.

Right in the text box you're already using.
The app needs to work with Fcitx5.

Ctrl+Alt
  1. 01

    Hold, and start talking

    Put the cursor in a text box and hold Ctrl+Alt for about 300 ms to start recording. If you're still composing pinyin, finish or cancel it first.

  2. 02

    Pause, and sentences form

    Interim text adjusts to context and is committed when you pause. While holding, you can keep recording and commit several sentences, with no default 30-second limit.

  3. 03

    Release to wrap up

    Release Ctrl or Alt to stop and commit the last sentence. Press Esc to discard uncommitted text; sentences already written stay. You can also toggle recording with Ctrl+Alt+V, which records up to 30 seconds at a time by default.

Package 0.4.0 · Sets itself up after install.
Ubuntu 26.04 · amd64 (x86-64)
Requires Fcitx5 5.1.19 or newer.

Install, and it sets itself up.

MIT licensed · Free to use and modify

Download the .deb and install it with the Software app. The light theme is bundled and enabled on first setup; existing custom themes and dark preferences are kept. The runtime, models and voice service are prepared automatically.

Download .deb ↓Release notes and checksums ↗

Finish anything you're typing before you install. Installation sets Fcitx5 as the default input method and restarts it, keeping your existing pinyin and voice settings.

First run

Stay online while about 260 MiB of models and the required dependencies download automatically. When the notification “语音输入已就绪” (Voice input is ready) appears, log out and log back in.

In any text box that works with Fcitx5, hold Ctrl + Alt to start talking and release to finish.

Or install from the terminal

Open a terminal in the folder where you downloaded the package and run:

sudo apt install ./fcitx5-voice_0.4.0_amd64.deb

The interface and documentation are currently in Chinese. For other distributions or ARM devices, see the build-from-source guide and verify it yourself. LiltKey is the product name; the command and config directory are still called fcitx5-voice.

GOOD TO KNOW.

Before you start,
worth knowing.

Is the interface available in English?

Not yet. Status messages, notifications and setup prompts are currently shown in Chinese only, for example 语音输入：录音中 (Voice input: recording) and 语音输入已就绪 (Voice input is ready). Dictation itself works in both Chinese and English.

Can I use, modify or redistribute the source code?

Yes. LiltKey's original code is released under the MIT License, which allows use, modification and redistribution as long as the copyright and license notice are kept. Dependencies and pretrained models follow their own terms; see third-party notices and model licenses.

Does it work in every Linux app?

It works in apps whose text fields work with Fcitx5. If the app supports client-side preedit, interim text appears at the cursor; otherwise it falls back to the input method panel. The current target is Ubuntu 26.04 with Fcitx5 5.1.19; other environments need to be rebuilt and verified. Not every desktop app has been tested with a real microphone.

Will it clash with other Ctrl+Alt shortcuts?

A short press of Ctrl+Alt doesn't start recording, and pressing any other key during the roughly 300 ms wait cancels it. Left and right Ctrl and Alt both work; AltGr doesn't count as Alt. Switching windows or text fields cancels the current session.

Does it affect my existing pinyin input?

Installation sets Fcitx5 as the default input method and restarts it, keeping your existing pinyin and voice settings. Finish or cancel any pinyin you're composing before you install, and log out and back in once setup is ready. While dictating, regular typing or switching windows or text fields cancels the current voice session. Voice input is disabled in password and other sensitive fields.

Will my theme change to the one in the screenshot?

First setup switches Fcitx5's default light theme to the LiltKey light theme. Custom themes, the default dark theme, a follow-system dark preference, non-default fonts and candidate layout are all kept, and upgrades never overwrite your later choices. You can switch themes manually in Fcitx 5 Configuration → Addons → Classic User Interface. The screenshot shows the real Fcitx5 pinyin panel; Kimpanel and panels drawn by individual apps don't use this theme.

What if the ready notification never shows up?

If no desktop session was running during installation, setup starts at your next login. First-time setup needs internet access; failed downloads retry every 5 minutes, and setup continues at the next login after you log out or shut down. There's no need to reinstall. Run journalctl --user -u fcitx5-voice-setup -n 50 to see progress and errors, or read installation and troubleshooting for more.

Are recognition and punctuation always accurate?

Recognition quality depends on the recording, the content and the model, and accuracy hasn't yet been validated against a dataset of real user dictation. Punctuation can be wrong too; it only handles the current sentence and never rewrites text that's already committed. Check important text before you send it.

Can I review the text before it's committed?

Yes. Switch to the retained SenseVoice offline preview mode: after recording, press Enter to commit or Backspace to delete the last character of the preview. This differs from the default streaming mode, which stops when you release the hold shortcut or press Ctrl+Alt+V again, with no Enter needed. The config file is ~/.config/fcitx5-voice/config.toml.

What are the current limitations?

Holding Ctrl+Alt records until you release; toggling with Ctrl+Alt+V records up to 30 seconds at a time by default. Noise suppression, personal hotwords, cloud recognition and automatic rewriting aren't provided. If you move the mouse within the same text field, how quickly the session is cancelled depends on the input method events the app sends. Pretrained models follow their own licenses.
